title: Cast on Elemental Ailment Guide — Trigger, Energy and Socketed Spell
summary: Cast on Elemental Ailment (CoEA) is the Meta trigger gem created in 0.3.0 by merging Cast on Freeze / Cast on Shock / Cast on Ignite. This guide explains why you can no longer find a standalone Cast on Freeze, how Freeze / Shock / Ignite each generate Energy, how your Socketed Spell's cast time sets the maximum Energy, why you see Missing Socketed Skill, and how to keep single-target bosses triggering.
description: Cast on Elemental Ailment deep guide: Energy formulas for Freeze / Shock / Ignite, maximum Energy vs Socketed Spell cast time, Mana behavior of triggered spells, how it differs from Elemental Invocation, common non-triggering causes with direct answers, mapping and boss rotations, recommended builds and real community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Overview: What CoEA Actually Does
paragraphs: Cast on Elemental Ailment is a Meta trigger gem: you socket a Spell into its Socketed Spell slot, and whenever your attacks or skills pile up enough elemental ailments (Freeze, Shock, Ignite) on enemies, the gem spends accumulated Energy to automatically cast that Spell. It is not a damage skill on its own — it is an engine that turns 'apply ailments' into 'auto-cast a Spell'.

Why can't you find Cast on Freeze anymore? In 0.3.0 GGG merged Cast on Freeze, Cast on Shock and Cast on Ignite into Cast on Elemental Ailment. The old names survive only as search aliases and migration notes; the current canonical page is CoEA. Any guide still telling you to socket a standalone 'Cast on Freeze' is outdated.

Its value is decoupling 'spreading ailments' from 'dealing burst': your main skill keeps applying ailments while CoEA automatically slams a high-damage Spell like Comet, Eye of Winter or Frost Wall at the right moment. The cost is Spirit reservation, a required Socketed Spell, and a trigger cadence that depends heavily on how efficiently you apply ailments.
bullets: Essence: an ailment-accumulation engine that auto-casts a Socketed Spell.
Origin: merged from Cast on Freeze / Shock / Ignite in 0.3.0; old names retired.
Energy currency: generated separately by Freeze, Shock and Ignite.
Key limits: needs a Socketed Spell, costs Spirit, cadence depends on ailment uptime.
Common traps: Missing Socketed Skill, no Energy gain, single-target boss stalls.

sections.title: Mechanics: Three Gems Into One
paragraphs: Merge logic: the old Cast on Freeze / Shock / Ignite each responded to one ailment. CoEA responds to all three, but each ailment contributes Energy under different rules. You no longer pick a gem based on 'I want to trigger on freeze' vs 'on ignite' — one CoEA eats Energy from all three.

Practical impact: the old 'Cast on Freeze mandatory' conclusion does not transfer directly. Now you care about which ailment your main skill reliably applies, and how fast, plus which ailment is most efficient in the current scenario. In dense maps Freeze triggers fastest; on a single boss where Freeze is hard to sustain, Shock or Ignite may be steadier.

Difference from Elemental Invocation: both touch ailments / elements but are different systems. CoEA is something you equip with a Spell socketed, auto-triggered by ailment accumulation; Elemental Invocation is a separate elemental-charge trigger system. Don't conflate them — pick one as your main trigger engine.
bullets: Old Cast on Freeze / Shock / Ignite merged into CoEA; standalone pages gone.
One CoEA responds to Freeze, Shock and Ignite simultaneously.
Each ailment's Energy efficiency differs; choose your main ailment by scenario.
Elemental Invocation is a different system; don't mix the two up.

sections.title: Energy Formula: How Each Ailment Builds Up
rows: 10 Energy per Freeze Power — awarded when you Freeze or fully build freeze on a target
Fastest in dense packs; best for clearing
Stalls on freeze-immune or phase-shifting bosses; needs freeze buildup or chilling ground
1 Energy per Shock Power — awarded each time you reach the Shock threshold
Medium; depends on shock threshold and shock magnitude
Stacking shock magnitude amplifies per-shock Energy; good for mid-speed multi-target
1 Energy per Ignite Power × ignite intensity ratio (intensity ÷ Ailment Threshold)
Tied to Ignite intensity / Ailment Threshold ratio
High ignite intensity sustains single-target; often paired with Flammability-style scaling

sections.title: Maximum Energy and Socketed Spell Cast Time
paragraphs: Energy is not infinite. CoEA has an internal maximum Energy cap, and that cap is set directly by the base cast time of the Socketed Spell you slot: Max Energy = 10 × (Socketed Spell cast time ÷ 0.1s). In other words, a 0.8s-cast Spell stores up to 80 Energy per socketed step; a 0.2s-cast Spell stores only 20. This is why many builds choose a relatively long-cast-time Spell — it decides 'how heavy a slam can I charge up'.

The cost is cadence: a long-cast-time Spell also triggers less often — high single hit, low frequency. A short-cast-time Spell triggers often but with a lower cap. Mapping usually prefers frequent small slams for faster clears; bossing prefers a fully charged heavy slam.

Triggered Spells still cost Mana: CoEA only 'auto-presses cast' for you; it does not waive the Spell's Mana cost. If your Socketed Spell is expensive, you need a Mana pool, recovery or aura that can sustain continuous auto-casts, or the auto-cast gets interrupted and you bottom out.
bullets: Max Energy cap scales with Socketed Spell cast time; long cast = high cap.
Long cast: heavy but infrequent; short cast: light but frequent.
Boss = charged slam, clear = fast slam is the common trade-off.
Triggered Spell still costs Mana; sustain your blue pool.

supports.label: Boundless Energy
notes: Directly raises Energy cap / gain efficiency; one of the most core CoEA supports.
Nearly every CoEA build runs it — it decides how full and how often you slam.

supports.label: Energy Retention
notes: Slows Energy decay or improves retention, widening the trigger window.
Especially valuable in boss stall scenarios.

supports.label: Considered Casting
notes: Improves trigger stability / effective cast time of the Socketed Spell; common pairing.
Exact benefit verified on current client.

supports.label: Spell Cascade
notes: Adds coverage to the triggered Spell, boosting clear speed.
Limited value on single-target bosses.

supports.label: Magnified Area
notes: Enlarges the triggered Spell's area, pairs with AoE Spells for clearing.
Little help on a pinned boss.

supports.label: Spell Echo
notes: Incompatible: a Triggered Spell is NOT re-triggered by Spell Echo; it only affects the same Spell when you cast it manually.
A common community mistake is treating Spell Echo as 'makes triggering faster' — it does not speed up triggers.

supports.label: Controlled Destruction
notes: Boosts the triggered Spell's direct damage, good for burst-focused Socketed Spells.
Drops crit; confirm your Spell doesn't rely on crit.

sections.title: Build Use Cases: Three Trigger Routes
paragraphs: Freeze-clear route: a high-frequency freeze main skill (e.g. Ice Nova / Frost Wall + cold attacks) with CoEA socketing Comet or Eye of Winter. Freeze triggers extremely fast in dense packs — ideal for speed clearing. Risk: freeze-immune or phase-shifting bosses stall.

Shock single-target route: steady Energy from high shock magnitude, good for mid-speed multi-target and some bosses. Requires actively stacking shock magnitude (shock threshold + shock multiplier) or efficiency is mediocre.

Ignite hybrid route: high ignite intensity (often with Flammability-style scaling) sustains single-target bosses that can't be frozen. Cost: ignite builds demand higher Ailment investment and are more single-purpose.
bullets: Freeze-clear: frequent freeze + Comet/Eye of Winter; fastest clear, boss-stall risk.
Shock ST: steady supply via shock magnitude; mid-speed multi-target friendly.
Ignite hybrid: high ignite intensity feeds single-target bosses; more specialized.
Cold Caster / Stormweaver are the most common CoEA carriers today.

sections.title: Common Mistakes: Why It Won't Trigger
paragraphs: Missing Socketed Skill: you have no Spell in CoEA's slot, or the Spell was removed / lives in another weapon set that isn't active. Direct answer: confirm the Socketed Spell slot holds exactly one valid Spell and the currently active weapon set also carries it.

Energy not rising: your ailment application is too weak, or the ailment type doesn't match. E.g. you rely on Freeze but fight a freeze-immune boss, so Energy naturally stalls. Direct answer: check which ailment your main skill actually applies and whether it triggers reliably on the current target.

Assuming Spirit is enough: enough Spirit is necessary, not sufficient. CoEA also consumes the Socketed Spell's cast resource, Mana, and a correct ailment source. Direct answer: verify Spell slot, Mana sustainability and ailment source together.

Minion ailments don't count: Freeze / Shock / Ignite dealt by minions or other non-self skills usually do not generate Energy for your CoEA. Direct answer: ailments must come from your own skill chain.
Thinking Spell Echo speeds triggers: as noted, a Triggered Spell is not re-triggered by Spell Echo. Direct answer: use Spell Echo on the manually cast same Spell, not to accelerate triggers.
bullets: Issue: Missing Socketed Skill.
Direct answer: slot must hold one valid Spell active in the current weapon set.
Issue: Energy stalls / single-target boss drops.
Direct answer: ailment source mismatches the target (e.g. freeze-immune boss); switch main ailment or route.
Issue: minion ailments don't count as Energy.
Direct answer: ailments must come from your own skills.

items.question: Why can't I find a Cast on Freeze gem?
answer: From 0.3.0 GGG merged Cast on Freeze / Shock / Ignite into Cast on Elemental Ailment.
The old names remain only as search aliases and migration notes; the current page is CoEA.

items.question: What decides the Energy cap?
answer: The base cast time of the Socketed Spell you slot: Max Energy = 10 × (cast time ÷ 0.1s).
A 0.8s-cast Spell stores up to 80 Energy; a 0.2s-cast Spell stores only 20.

items.question: Does the triggered Spell still cost Mana?
answer: Yes. CoEA only auto-casts; it does not waive the Spell's Mana cost.
Mana-tight builds need a pool, recovery or aura to sustain continuous auto-casts.

items.question: Do minion Freeze / Shock / Ignite count for my Energy?
answer: Usually no. Energy comes from ailments your own skill chain applies.
Ailments from minions or other non-self skills generally do not generate Energy for CoEA.

items.question: How do I keep single-target bosses triggering?
answer: Single-target bosses that resist Freeze stall your Energy; switch your main ailment route. Use high Ignite intensity (often with Flammability-style scaling) or stack Shock magnitude to keep Energy flowing.
Also run the Energy Retention support and pick a longer-cast-time Socketed Spell so each charge is heavier and the trigger window is wider.

items.question: What is the best Socketed Spell for CoEA?
answer: It depends on your route. Freeze-clear builds commonly socket Comet or Eye of Winter for fast packs, while Ignite or Shock single-target routes may prefer a heavier Spell you can fully charge.
Match the Socketed Spell's cast time to your goal: a long cast gives a high Energy cap and a heavy slam, a short cast gives frequent light slams.

items.question: How is CoEA different from Elemental Invocation?
answer: Both touch ailments and elements but are separate systems. CoEA is a gem you equip with a Spell socketed; it auto-casts that Spell once ailment Energy fills.
Elemental Invocation is a different elemental-charge trigger system — pick one as your main trigger engine rather than mixing the two.
